title: On Fairy-Stories
container_title: Essays Presented to Charles Williams; later reprinted in Tree and Leaf / The Monsters and the Critics and Other Essays
evidence_note: Primary source for sub-creation, secondary world, secondary belief, and inner consistency; cite an authoritative print edition and page numbers in formal scholarship.
report_use: Conceptual foundation; not treated as a contemporary European practice by itself.

title: Building Imaginary Worlds: The Theory and History of Subcreation
evidence_note: Cross-media framework for imaginary worlds; world-building extends beyond plot and includes world structures, audience engagement, transmedial growth, and authorship.
report_use: World/story distinction, world components, consistency, completeness, transmediality.

title: Notes Toward a Critical Approach to Worlds and World-Building
container_title: Fafnir – Nordic Journal of Science Fiction and Fantasy Research
evidence_note: Clarifies authorial, readerly, and critical world-building; proposes topofocal analysis and analysis of interrelated building blocks.
report_use: Spatial architecture, analytical vocabulary, caution against using world-building as an imprecise catch-all.

title: Imaginative, Immersive and Interactive Engagements: The Rhetoric of Worldbuilding in Contemporary Speculative Fiction
evidence_note: Treats speculative world-building as rhetorical/communicative practice across media; engagement organized around imagination, immersion, and interaction.
report_use: Reader/player engagement, rhetorical framing, estrangement, cross-media perspective.

title: Transmedial Worlds – Rethinking Cyberworld Design
container_title: Proceedings of the 2004 International Conference on Cyberworlds
evidence_note: Introduces transmedial world and worldness; commonly summarized through mythos, topos, and ethos.
report_use: Shared world identity, canon stewardship, cross-platform architecture.

title: Worlds from Words: Theories of World-building as Creative Writing Toolbox
container_title: World Building: Discourse in the Mind, edited by Joanna Gavins and Ernestine Lahey
evidence_note: Connects cognitive poetics, Text-World Theory, Possible Worlds Theory, and creative practice; discusses description, defamiliarization, reader trust, and narrative voice.
report_use: Prose techniques and audience inference; specific chapter is available as a repository preprint/final proof.

title: Rhetorics of Fantasy
evidence_note: Fantasy taxonomy organized around portal-quest, immersive, intrusion, and liminal rhetorical modes; these are modes of address/entry, not a universal quality scale.
report_use: Entry-point and disclosure strategies for fantasy worlds.

title: World Building: Transmedia, Fans, Industries
evidence_note: Open-access collection on theories, industry, immersion, media as world-building devices, and fan appropriations; includes chapters on proliferation, maps, games, sound, comics, and authorship.
report_use: Transmedia, visual/sonic world cues, participatory and industrial dimensions.

title: Critical Worldbuilding: Toward a Geographical Engagement with Imagined Worlds
evidence_note: Frames imagined worlds as political artifacts and calls for geographic and critical engagement; connects world-building with social, cultural, and environmental relations.
report_use: Place, political ecology, critical world-building and representation audit.

title: Building Possible Worlds: A Speculation Based Framework to Reflect on Images of the Future
evidence_note: Proposes speculative world-building as a participatory method for thickly describing possible worlds to surface present assumptions and reflect on current choices.
report_use: Future scenario methods, speculative design, workshop facilitation; not evidence for prediction accuracy.

title: World-Building as Grand-Scale Speculation: Planetary, Cosmic and Conceptual Thought Experiments in Emmi Itäranta’s The Moonday Letters
container_title: Fafnir – Nordic Journal of Science Fiction and Fantasy Research
evidence_note: Case study of Finnish author Emmi Itäranta; discusses world-modelling, scale, Anthropocene/global ethics, and world as a heuristic model.
report_use: Scale shifts, planetary/ecological systems, linking speculative models to real-world interpretation.

title: Contemporary European Science Fiction Cinemas
evidence_note: Study of twenty-first-century European SF cinema and crisis narratives, including financial crisis, political extremism, migration, climate change, multiculturalism, and European identity.
report_use: European-specific context; illustrates that speculative futures can model contemporary political concerns.

title: Imaginative, Immersive and Interactive Engagements: The Rhetoric of Worldbuilding in Contemporary Speculative Fiction (lectio praecursoria)
container_title: Fafnir – Nordic Journal of Science Fiction and Fantasy Research
evidence_note: Concise author-presented summary of the 2016 Tampere doctoral dissertation; useful alongside, not instead of, the dissertation.
report_use: Accessible summary of world-building as rhetorical practice.

title: Worldbuilding in Role-Playing Games
container_title: Role-Playing Game Studies: Transmedia Foundations, edited by José P. Zagal and Sebastian Deterding
evidence_note: Reviews models, components, processes, tensions, and practices of world-building with special attention to role-playing games.
report_use: Playable situation design, shared authorship, modular hooks and player-created narrative.

title: A Narrative Theory of Games
container_title: Proceedings of the International Conference on the Foundations of Digital Games
evidence_note: Differentiates game-world, objects, agents, and events and considers how game structures configure narrative possibilities.
report_use: Game-space topology, agency, event structure, and medium-specific design.

title: Persuasive Games: The Expressive Power of Videogames
evidence_note: Develops procedural rhetoric: games can make arguments through rule-based representation and interaction.
report_use: System-level and rule-based world claims; interpretive use should be paired with critiques and close analysis.

title: The Voices of Game Worlds: A Sociolinguistic Analysis of Disco Elysium
evidence_note: Analyzes how character voices and accents evoke class, ethnicity, privilege, and conflict in the Estonian-developed game Disco Elysium.
report_use: Sociolinguistic characterization, voice as world-cue, and ethical analysis of stereotyping.

title: From colonialist boardgames to radiocomputer wizardry: Investigating Disco Elysium’s intermedial world via media archaeology
container_title: Intermedial Networks: The Digital Present and Beyond (conference book of abstracts)
peer_reviewed: conference_abstract; review status not established from landing page
evidence_note: Analyzes fictional documents, stained glass, radios, pinball, computers, and board games as media-archaeological world cues in Disco Elysium.
report_use: In-world artifacts, technological history, and intermedial exposition; treated as a case source, not a full-length article.

title: World-Builders on World-Building: An Exploration of Subcreation
evidence_note: Collection combining academic accounts and creators' reflections on process and practice.
report_use: Practice-facing triangulation; label creator testimony separately from scholarly generalization.

title: Speculative Fiction
evidence_note: Surveys competing historical definitions of speculative fiction and treats it as an umbrella category in some scholarly uses.
report_use: Terminology and genre boundaries; avoid presenting one definition as universally accepted.

title: Where no European has gone before: Representations of Europe(an integration) in science fiction
evidence_note: Surveys European integration in science fiction across novels, films, and bandes dessinées; reports categories including surveillance, conspiracy, environmental disaster, and space exploration.
report_use: European identity as a speculative world element; bibliographic details should be checked against the journal version before formal citation.

title: Possible Worlds Theory and Contemporary Narratology
evidence_note: Updates possible-worlds approaches and applies them to contemporary fiction, digital fiction, games, graphic novels, historical narratives, and drama.
report_use: Actual/fictional-world relations, world accessibility, and cross-media analytic vocabulary.
